overview: This file consists of a British Embassy letter conveying unconfirmed intelligence about Japanese merchant shipping amid the deteriorating situation in the Far East. Nevile Butler informs U.S. State Department official Stanley K. Hornbeck that the British Foreign Office had received a report, passed by the Governor of New Caledonia to General Charles de Gaulle, that officers of Japanese merchant vessels said all Japanese ships had been ordered to return to Japan by March 1, 1941. The Foreign Office cautioned that the report had not been confirmed by other sources.

subfiles.about: Butler relays an unconfirmed report that all Japanese ships had been ordered to return to Japan by March 1, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Butler reports that the British Foreign Office had received a telegram concerning intelligence supplied by the Governor of New Caledonia to General de Gaulle. According to information attributed to officers of Japanese merchant vessels, all Japanese ships had been instructed to return to Japan by March 1. The Foreign Office emphasized that it had obtained no confirmation from other sources.

interest: The letter preserves an early, explicitly unconfirmed intelligence report about a general recall of Japanese shipping months before Japan entered the wider Pacific War. It is useful for studying how maritime rumors and observations from merchant officers moved through Free French, British, and American diplomatic channels. The Foreign Office's caveat about the absence of corroboration also illustrates the caution with which governments evaluated such reports.
